correctness.rationale: Every white set is explicitly computed from the original neighborhood rule. Singleton/pair failure and the n=5 exception are proved; every nonstar triple has at most two white pairs and is forced; all stars of size at least three are forced exactly when at most three spokes remain. Monotonicity covers every larger set. Polynomial terms are uniquely centered star counts; inclusion-minimal classes are separately proved. The finite verifier directly ran the original process on 2,278,600 configurations but does not stand in for the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: Prior published Kneser work supplies static three-vertex domination and zero-forcing invariants, while the inspected general power-domination polynomial and upper-minimal-set papers do not derive the exact Kneser two-subset all-set criterion. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not uniqueness from search absence; unindexed equivalent statements remain possible.

value.rationale: Provides the entire selected-set feasibility criterion and coefficient distribution for the canonical 2-subset Kneser graph, not just an easy minimum bound. Detects an unbounded spread between minimum and upper inclusion-minimal sizes n>=8 and exact cancellation yielding C(C(n,2),3) minimal sets. Both family and invariant are intrinsically natural, and the structural dichotomy identifies power-propagation behavior unavailable from static domination values.
